what_shipped_this_turn_1_the_launcher: cad395e and 66b62af. --detach makes a phase outlive its session; it does not make it CONTINUE. The controller's runner is subprocess.run on the argv it was given, so a trainer launched as a bare phase command (a) restarts at step zero on a retry, over the checkpoint the previous attempt wrote, (b) does the same on a relaunch after the session, the controller or the box died, and (c) writes no inflight.json -- which is what boot_resume continues a run from after a reboot and what session_keeper.supervised_job_probe reads to know the GPU is taken. Until that marker exists the keeper reads the box as FREE and keeps launching sessions beside the run. Phases 3-7 escaped this only because each had an orchestrator wrapping run_with_resume; phase 8 has the longest runs in the program and no orchestrator, and three handoffs in a row recorded 'whatever gets written for it must use the same primitive' -- a note asking the next author to remember. It is now in the launcher instead.
how_to_launch_phase_8_training: daedalus-approved phase run-phase --phase <name> --estimated-hours <h> --detach --log runs/<area>/<name>.log --supervise-checkpoint runs/<name>/checkpoint.pt --watchdog-tokens <target-tokens> --max-attempts 3 -- python train.py --run-name <name> ... . --supervise-checkpoint routes the phase through run_with_resume (marker written, interrupted run resumed on attempt one, --resume added on a retry, watchdog halt NOT resumed). --watchdog-tokens starts watchdog.py for divergence and stalls; omit it and the run has neither. --max-attempts and --backoff-sec become the SUPERVISOR's budget and backoff defaults to 60s there rather than 0. Full section in ops/vast/RUNBOOK.md, 'Launching a training phase so it can be continued'.
three_refusals_you_may_hit: (1) a supervised command carrying its own --resume is refused -- on attempt one it restores the finished run's step count so the phase trains nothing and exits 0; use --init-from to start from existing weights. (2) a --supervise-checkpoint that is not the path the command's train.py will write is refused, asked of train.checkpoint_path_for rather than composed; the phase 5 smoke found what composing costs. It is checked only when the command is a train.py carrying --run-name, so a sweep script or an evaluation pass is never blocked. (3) an undetached phase estimated at 0.25h or more is still refused as before.
